title: Autologous Hair Follicle-Derived Secretome and Platelet-Rich Plasma for Premature Ovarian Insufficiency
official: Does the Secretome From Autologous Hair Follicle-derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells Improve Ovarian Reserve in Women With Premature Ovarian Insufficiency?
summary:
This single-arm, open-label pilot study aims to evaluate changes in ovarian function following administration of autologous hair follicle-derived mesenchymal stem cell secretome combined with autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) in women with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI).

The study plans to enroll 15 women aged 25-40 years with evidence of diminished ovarian activity, including elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), low anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), and reduced antral follicle count (AFC).

The intervention is administered under transvaginal ultrasound guidance into the pelvic cul-de-sac, without direct ovarian injection. Participants undergo serial hormonal and ultrasound assessments to evaluate changes in FSH, AMH, and AFC. Secondary assessments include menstrual function, ovulation, and pregnancy outcomes.

The study is exploratory and is intended to generate preliminary data on ovarian response, feasibility, and safety to inform future controlled investigations.

interventions.name: Autologous Hair Follicle-Derived Secretome Combined With Platelet-Rich Plasma

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women aged 25-40 years.
* Diagnosis of premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), defined by an antral follicle count (AFC) of fewer than 5.
* Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) level below 3 pmol/L.
* Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) level above 30 IU/L on two occasions at least one month apart.
* Not receiving other medical or fertility treatments, except natural estrogen for the management of menopausal symptoms.
* Able and willing to provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Women older than 40 years.
* History of autoimmune disorders.
* History of hematopoietic cell malignancies.
* Medical conditions that would preclude infertility treatment or pregnancy, including HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B or C, or breast cancer.
* Body mass index (BMI) greater than 40 kg/m².
